title: The Open Ending
text:
Clara had read the short story many times before she noticed the final line. The author had left the ending open, which frustrated some readers who wanted a clear resolution. In the first paragraph, the narrator describes a quiet village where nothing ever seems to change. Clara, however, found the open ending hopeful.

Later, she discussed the story with her classmates. Most of them preferred a conclusion that explained what happened to the main character. Clara argued that a closed ending would have limited the reader's imagination. By the end of the discussion, the group agreed that the story had been effective, even though they did not agree about its meaning.

questions.text: In the first paragraph, what does the narrator describe?
options: A quiet village where nothing seems to change
A busy city with many new buildings
A school where students argue every day
A ship travelling across a stormy sea

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, what did most classmates prefer?
options: An open ending with no answers
A story set in a big city
A conclusion that explained what happened to the main character
A shorter version of the text

questions.text: Why does Clara find the open ending hopeful?
options: It leaves room for the reader's own imagination
It confirms the main character's fate
It makes the village seem more lively
It removes the need for any discussion

questions.text: What can be inferred about the group at the end of the discussion?
options: They valued the story even though they disagreed
They decided to rewrite the ending together
They agreed on one correct meaning

vocabulary.definition: annoyed because something prevents what one wants
a final solution or ending to a problem
the ability to create images or ideas in the mind

paragraph_translations: Clara tinha lido o conto muitas vezes antes de reparar na última frase. O autor deixou o final em aberto, o que frustrou alguns leitores que queriam uma resolução clara. No primeiro parágrafo, o narrador descreve uma aldeia tranquila onde nada parece mudar. Clara, no entanto, achou o final em aberto esperançoso.

Mais tarde, ela discutiu o conto com os colegas. A maioria preferia uma conclusão que explicasse o que aconteceu com a personagem principal. Clara argumentou que um final fechado limitaria a imaginação do leitor. No fim da discussão, o grupo concordou que o conto tinha sido eficaz, embora não concordasse sobre o seu significado.
